rows.why: No item asks what the default share is or what the basic hidden-tests release looks like. Item 1 is about rounding and item 3 is about rejecting invalid shares; neither settles that a 10000 bounty at the default share releases 7500 and becomes 'partially released'.

Item 1 asks how a fractional share is rounded. The pick rounds the hidden-test part down using BigInt integer division and gives the remainder to UAT (101 → 75/26). At 999 that gives 749/250, and BigInt keeps the result exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

Item 9 asks how the UAT release amount is computed. The pick releases the bounty minus earlier releases, which is the remaining balance. The run returned uat 90 after a hidden-tests release of 10, with status 'fully released'.
Item 10 asks what a failed hidden-test run does. The run returned status 'locked' with no releases and 0 writes.
Item 6 asks about UAT approval before the hidden tests pass. The run rejected with 'cannot approve UAT: the hidden tests have not passed', made 0 writes, and the store stayed undefined.
Item 5 asks what a bounty of 0 does. The status is 'pro bono', but the run recorded releases of amount 0 for both hidden-tests and uat. The scenario says no release is ever recorded.

Item 7 asks about a repeated hidden-tests pass. The pick ignores any later pass once a hidden-tests release exists, whatever its id, so the same id and a different id are both covered. The run made only 1 write and kept a single release.

Item 11 asks how concurrent events are handled, including through different handlers on the same store. The pick runs them one at a time through a per-store queue. The run sent concurrent duplicate passes through two handlers against a slow store and got exactly one hidden-tests release and one uat release. With items 7 and 8, the serialised duplicates (different ids, repeated UAT) record nothing.
Item 12 asks about a store write failure. The run rejected with 'disk', left the store undefined, and the retry of the same event succeeded with a 75 release.
